notes: Two documents (Provost taskforce syllabus guide; Academic Integrity students guide); both stance delegates. Main disagreement kinds: (1) policy_type on borderline units: P31 vs P53 for the bias sentence, P58 vs P19 for discussion-board posts, P24 vs P27 for 'indicate what part was written by AI', P30 vs P34 for 'asked to explain how you used these tools', P02 vs P44 for 'you will be asked to use AI to explore', P56 vs P60 for the MLA 'rather than surveil' line, P25 vs P24 for the disclosure paragraph, UNCOVERED vs P37 for departments' penalty conversations; each resolved by re-reading the sentence against the type definition (P27 is code-specific, P60 needs a statement that staff will not police, P53 is for harms rather than critical evaluation). (2) modality: 'it is important that' coded should not must; informs for institutional intentions and instructor commitments; violation declarations coded must-not; plain imperative 'speak with me' coded must. (3) unit_stance on accountability and disclosure units: responsibility and verification neutral, disclosure require. (4) actor: the sample-statement offering is admin; 'you' statements are student. (5) granularity: coder B merged consecutive sentences (penalty conversations, conference plus repeat offences, detection plus conference, fact-check plus responsibility, disclosure paragraph plus prompts); merged policies were split so each unit holds one rule, which is why 6 of A's and 5 of B's single-coder units were kept. Dropped single-coder units: A: guide purpose line and the duplicated half of the 'opportunities' sentence; B: a generic syllabus checklist question and six general integrity-procedure units that do not mention AI. Shares are over the 69 matched units.
